spec_match.rationale: The controller reads the exact WheelEvent.momentum member and never substitutes a timer heuristic when it is absent.

interactive.rationale: Wheel input changes a real zoom surface; users can compare apply, dampen, and ignore policies, reset state, and inspect event classifications.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index describes the practical map/CAD/data-canvas overshoot problem and the controls delivered by the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported browsers keep accessible zoom controls, classify wheel input as unknown rather than inferred momentum, and disable only the unavailable policy selector.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus and the canonical Pointer Events WheelEvent section are directly linked.

conformance.rationale: The inherited suite tests the exact prototype member and native event property; its failures remain visibly honest in pre-151 Chrome.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chrome DevTools MCP at 390×844 and 1280×800 exercised zoom in/out/reset and a wheel event, verified unknown fallback behavior, exact widths, and clean console/network.

telemetry_health.rationale: Wheel interactions emit a privacy-safe assertion that verifies native values are boolean when the member is supported.

design_system.rationale: The responsive tool uses shared variables, intrinsic grids, and reduced-motion-aware transforms.

accessibility.rationale: The zoom surface is keyboard-focusable and named, every control is native and labelled, non-wheel zoom buttons are available, and classifications have text equivalents.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The tool collapses to one column at 390px and uses two columns at 1280px with no document overflow or clipped controls.

openQuestions.title: Validate real trackpad momentum on Chrome 151 hardware
openQuestions.detail: Use a physical trackpad fling in Chrome 151+ and capture direct versus momentum counts under apply, dampen, and ignore policies. Constructed WheelEvents are not native-input proof.

openQuestions.title: Add an expensive-render commit planner
openQuestions.detail: Demonstrate low-quality preview rendering during momentum and one high-quality commit after the inertial tail, with measured work avoided.

guidanceConsulted.query: Build an accessible wheel-controlled map zoom interaction with keyboard controls and reduced motion
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Do not make pointer input the only path; use native labelled controls, textual state, visible focus, and motion-preference-aware presentation.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Added named focusable canvas, zoom buttons, labelled policy selector, textual metrics/event log, and reduced-motion-aware transition behavior.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: MCP exercised the non-wheel controls and inspected the complete fallback and visible live-test state at both viewport classes.

summary: Adds the missing product utility layer: a real zoom-controller decision that shows why classifying inertial tail events matters, while remaining honest on pre-151 browsers.
